title: Text tools
hook: Clean, fix, cut and join text, like tidying a messy call sheet.

warmup.explain: You look up with the key and get the value. The key is a, the value is 1.
len counts the items. Three items, so 3.

warmup.q: You type `7` into an `input()`. Python holds it as...
warmup.explain: input always gives text. Use int() when you need the number.

why.heading: Real text is messy
why.text: Names arrive as `  sam dube `, in capitals, with spaces at the ends. File names are `clip_01.mov` when you want `ICL_01.mp4`. Python has small **methods** that tidy text. A method is a tool that belongs to the text, written after a dot.

why.heading: Tidy tools
why.text:
`.strip()` removes spaces from both ends.
`.lower()` makes all small letters. `.upper()` all capitals.
`.title()` makes Each Word Start With A Capital.

They give back a NEW text. Your original is not changed, so print it or save it: `name = name.strip()`

why.heading: Replace, split, join
why.text:
`"clip_01".replace("clip", "ICL")` swaps one piece for another.

`"Sam Dube".split(" ")` cuts text into a list: `['Sam', 'Dube']`.

`"-".join(parts)` glues a list back into text, with `-` between. The text before `.join` is the glue.

why.heading: Ask questions about text
why.text:
`in` works on text too: `"mp4" in filename` is True or False.

`len("hello")` counts the characters: 5.

You can chain tools: `raw.strip().title()` strips first, then fixes the capitals.

why.heading: Slicing: take a piece
why.text: Text counts from 0, just like a list. `name[0]` is the first letter. `name[:3]` takes everything up to (not including) spot 3, so the first three letters. Leave out the first number and it starts at the beginning.

watch.intro: Tap Run. One messy name and one file name, cleaned up.
watch.code:
raw = "  thandi DUBE "
name = raw.strip().title()
print(name)
print(name.upper())
print(len(name))
print(name[:3])
parts = name.split(" ")
print(parts)
print("-".join(parts))
print("Dube" in name)
print("clip_01.mp4".replace("clip", "ICL"))
explain: `strip` removed the spaces, then `title` fixed the capitals. Two tools chained.
`len` counted 11 characters, and `[:3]` took the first three.
`split` made a list of two words, and `join` glued them with a dash.
watch.break_it: Break it on purpose: change `name.upper()` to `name.uper()` (missing p) and tap Run. The error says `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'uper'`. That means: text has no tool with that name. Check the spelling.

tasks.title: Tidy one name
tasks.task:
The name is messy. Print it tidy, with no spaces at the ends and a capital letter on each word:

`Sipho Naidoo`
tasks.starter:
name = "  sIPHO naidoo  "
# print it tidy
hints: Two tools: one removes the spaces at the ends, one fixes the capitals.

tasks.title: Rename the clips
tasks.task:
The clips are named `clip_01.mov`. Loop through the list and print each name with `clip` swapped for `ICL`:

`ICL_01.mov`
`ICL_02.mov`
`ICL_03.mov`
tasks.starter:
files = ["clip_01.mov", "clip_02.mov", "clip_03.mov"]
# loop and print the new names
hints: You need a for loop over files, and .replace inside it.
for f in files: then an indented print.

tasks.title: Name and initials
tasks.task:
Ask `Full name? ` (two words, any capitals). Print the name tidy in title case, then the initials like `T.D.`. Example with `thandi dube`:

`Full name? thandi dube`
`Thandi Dube`
`T.D.`
tasks.starter:
name = input("Full name? ")
# tidy it, print it, then print the initials
tasks.solution:
name = input("Full name? ")
name = name.strip().title()
print(name)
parts = name.split(" ")
print(f"{parts[0][0]}.{parts[1][0]}.")
hints: First fix the name with .title(). Then .split(" ") gives you a list of the two words.
The first letter of a word is word[0]. So parts[0][0] is the first letter of the first word.

tests.expect:
Full name? thandi dube
Thandi Dube
T.D.

Full name? lebo MOKOENA
Lebo Mokoena
L.M.

recap: `.replace(a, b)` swaps pieces. `.split(" ")` makes a list, `" ".join(list)` makes text.
`in` and `len` work on text. `text[:3]` takes the first three characters.
Text tools give back new text. Save it or print it.

words.meaning: A tool that belongs to a thing, written after a dot, like name.upper().
Remove spaces from the start and end of text.
Cut text into a list at a chosen spot.
Glue a list of text together with a separator.
A piece of text or a list, like name[:3].
